fatal_errors: The proposed material is initially single-phase CoCrFeMnNi, whereas the target system is as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 domains.
The proposed 300–500 °C aging window misses the target 550–750 °C window and the critical embrittlement and recovery temperatures near 600 °C and 750 °C.
The hypothesis assigns embrittlement to generic intragranular chemical clusters rather than coupled L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary evolution.
It does not predict the defining non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition or high-temperature ductility recovery.
Al addition changes the alloy composition and introduces a separate processing route, preventing a clean reconstruction of the controlled thermal-aging comparison.
No prior evidence is cited to establish that the proposed clusters form or control toughness in this material class.
explanation: The response addresses the broad question of non-grain-boundary embrittlement in a compositionally complex alloy and offers measurable controls, microscopy, mechanical testing, and a nominal falsification rule. There is limited conceptual overlap because ordering or clustering is proposed to impede dislocations and lower ductility. However, it reconstructs neither the material nor the central mechanism. The target concerns a dual-phase eutectic HEA in which aging near 600 °C maximizes L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundaries; elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at boundary tips produce plastic instability. Aging near 750 °C reduces ordering and creates ductile transition zones, restoring ductility. The generated hypothesis instead predicts broadly monotonic degradation from intragranular clusters in another alloy and temperature range. Its experiment could test its own idea, but it lacks the decisive target measurements of dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips, and the two intervention routes introduce avoidable compositional confounding. Without supporting evidence, it is an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
